title: Internationalized placeholder strategy and dynamic label collapse for metric cards
creator: Elena Ortiz
description: Design a robust strategy for metric card placeholders and a dynamic label collapse pattern that works across locales and screen sizes. The goal is to ensure number formatting, units, and truncated labels remain accessible to screen reader users, keyboard operable, and resilient across RTL and verbose languages. This ticket covers the pattern spec, prototypes, developer tokens for collapsed states, keyboard behavior, and allowed microcopy variants for translations.
background: We observed inconsistent placeholder states and label truncation in per-route and per-model metric cards during long label translations (Turkish, German, Japanese). Screen reader users receive ambiguous context when numeric values are delayed by network batching and caching; keyboard users cannot reliably expand collapsed labels. Existing truncation uses ellipses only and lacks semantic announcements and explicit expand affordances.
goals: Provide an accessible placeholder pattern for delayed metrics that announces loading state with localized phrasing
Define a deterministic label collapse policy (when to collapse, where to show tooltips, how to allow keyboard expansion)
Ensure numeric and currency formatting follows user locale and approximation semantics (e.g., ~1.2k vs 1,200) with clear SR announcements
Ship a small, RTL-safe CSS token set and aria pattern for collapsed/expanded states to hand to frontend engineers
acceptance_criteria: When values are pending, screen readers read: ‘Metric name — loading — value pending’ in the user locale
Collapsed labels expose a visible expand control (icon button) focusable by keyboard and reachable in the logical DOM order
Expanded label state persists for the keyboard focus session (not lost when card rerenders) and has aria-expanded toggle state
Numbers displayed follow CLDR locale rules (decimal separators, grouping) and abbreviated forms include accessible expanded text (e.g., visually “1.2k” SR reads “1,200 tokens”)
RTL locales mirror icon placement and maintain a logical reading order for SR/navigation
Design tokens and examples provided for 4 density breakpoints and two contrast ramps (AA and AAA target where feasible)
qa_checklist: Keyboard navigation: tab order includes the expand control and announces state
Screen reader: VoiceOver (macOS), NVDA (Windows), TalkBack (Android) verify announcements in English + two non-latin locales
Localization: Verify translations for loading microcopy in FR, TR, JA, DE
Contrast: Validate collapsed label background / icon meet AA for normal text and AAA for large text where applicable
Performance: Ensure placeholder strategy prevents layout shift above 0.1 CLS threshold on metric lists
accessibility_tests: Automated axe-core runs on storybook stories added; failures tracked in QA board
Manual focus order checks across density and narrow-breakpoint list views
localization_issues: Long-label wrap rules: allow multi-line labels up to 2 lines before collapse (locale-dependent)
Numeric abbreviation policy: translators must have expanded-clause to provide plural/suffix rules
Fallback phrasing when translation missing: en-US fallback must not be more than two words longer than localized version to avoid layout breakage
decisions: Use explicit expand icon (icon-only is permitted only with aria-label and visible focus ring)
Abbreviated numbers render visually but include hidden element with full number for SR that toggles with aria-live when value updates
Loading phrasing will be localized strings: 'loading', 'chargement', 'yükleniyor', '読み込み中' delivered via i18n catalog key console.metrics.loading
implementation_notes: Frontend: add data-attributes for collapsed state and provide a small JS utility to persist expandedness in sessionStorage keyed by card id
Backend: ensure endpoints return both formatted and raw numeric values to allow SR-friendly expansion without reformatting on the client
Tokens: add token --metric-label-max-lines, --metric-collapse-icon-size, and contrast ramp variables in tokens/metrics.json
